root_cause.text: In `fs/btrfs/inode.c::btrfs_create_new_inode()`, Btrfs only discovered oversized same-hash directory entries during `btrfs_add_link()` after tree updates had already begun, so a directory-item leaf-size overflow from name hash collisions escalated into a transaction abort instead of a clean `-ENOSPC`-style failure.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early `btrfs_check_dir_item_collision(BTRFS_I(dir)->root, btrfs_ino(BTRFS_I(dir)), name)` check “before we call `btrfs_add_link()`” specifically “to avoid a transaction abort” when “we have an existing dir item due to existing name hash collisions,” and the CVE description says the overflow “trigger[s] a transaction abort and turns the filesystem into RO mode.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an early directory-item collision check in btrfs inode creation to prevent dir item overflow and transaction aborts.
intent_record.what: In btrfs_create_new_inode(), a new pre-check was inserted before path allocation: when the request is neither for an orphan nor a subvolume, the code now calls btrfs_check_dir_item_collision() with the parent directory root, parent inode number, and name. If that call returns a negative error, the function returns immediately. The added block includes comments explaining that this is done before btrfs_add_link() to avoid dir item overflow and a transaction abort; subvolume creation is explicitly excluded because it is already checked in btrfs_mksubvol().
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now detects potentially problematic directory item collisions earlier in the inode creation flow and aborts with an error before attempting to add the link. This prevents a later dir item overflow that could otherwise trigger a transaction abort, improving robustness and closing a potential maliciously-triggered failure path. Subvolume creation behavior is unchanged because it already performs the equivalent validation elsewhere.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds an early same-hash directory-entry collision check during inode creation to prevent dir-item leaf-size overflow and avoid a later transaction abort.
